name: Ambrosia

project_scope.selection_mode: Asteraceae batch 3 — ragweeds, thistles, and common roadside species

study_strategy.warning: This batch includes several groups where flower color alone is weak; use leaf and involucre characters.

curation_status.visual_status: comparison built; diagnostic macro photographs pending

look_here_first: Find dangling staminate heads at the stem tip and small pistillate heads below. Compare mid-stem leaves: palmate 3–5 lobes suggests A. trifida; pinnately divided leaves require the annual-vs-rhizomatous A. artemisiifolia/A. psilostachya split.
shared_traits: Separate male and female flower heads on the same plant; terminal male spikes and smaller female heads below.
Female involucre surrounds a single fruit and persists as a bur.

comparison_matrix.artemisiifolia: Small with several short sharp spines
comparison_matrix.psilostachya: Small with blunt or absent tubercles

comparison_matrix.artemisiifolia: Terminal male heads above axillary female heads
comparison_matrix.psilostachya: Terminal male heads above axillary female heads
comparison_matrix.trifida: Same arrangement; sometimes dark-veined male involucres

overlap_cautions: A. artemisiifolia and A. psilostachya leaf dissection and bur spines overlap; confirm rhizomes and mature burs.
A. trifida can have unlobed leaves; inspect multiple nodes.
Height and color are not decisive.
lookalikes: Iva annua: inspect leaf dissection and male/female head arrangement.
Iva angustifolia: narrow leaves; compare reproductive heads.
Xanthium strumarium: broad leaves and large paired hooked burs.
Parthenium hysterophorus: finely dissected leaves but small heads with tiny white rays.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched mid-stem leaf views with lobe origin labeled for all three.
Annual root versus western-ragweed creeping rhizome.
Three mature female burs with millimeter scale and spine/tubercle labels.
Same-plant terminal male versus axillary female head close-ups.
Lower and upper stem nodes showing leaf arrangement.
Matched whole-plant habit and colonies with scale.
